title: Q: Cover ordinary and support access to setup progress
public_pr_body:
Q found no test for ordinary-user/support access to saved setup progress: the existing DB test covers cross-company admins only. Add eight DB-free tests: real React guide checks office/workshop/viewer, read-only and elevated support, mismatched company, own-admin edits and loss of access on entering support; plus a security contract check for every SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE policy clause in the unapplied proposal.

Four new UI cases failed before the correction. The guide now requires the matching own-company session, active admin role, and explicit non-support/non-read-only state before loading or showing saved progress. SQL/RLS is unchanged and remains the final permission boundary. The contract test checks company/admin/support constraints in all read/write clauses; it does not claim to execute PostgreSQL policies.

Based on combined N #236 (codex/n-company-setup-email-combined). Diff only components/company-setup-guide.tsx and tests/unit/company-setup-access.test.ts. No existing test weakened.

Validation: 12 setup unit tests passed, typecheck and targeted lint passed. Real DB policy checks remain NOT RUN; no SQL applied, browser/live provider checks, deployment, merge or Ready label.


Q coverage audit: two previously missing explicit cases were setup ordinary/support access (#239: 12 setup units passed including the new policy/UI cases) and Company B reading A's new-provider status/balance (#240: 9 accounting units passed). Remaining conditions already have tests: chase-approve/chase-approval-ui on #233 passed 48; tolra-ai, ai-mode-key-isolation, tolra-ai-caps, tolra-ai-caps-ui and tolra-ai-controls-ui on #234 passed 43. N's 5,138-test run includes legacy email round-trips, read-only editor behaviour and paid-break/timesheet comparisons. The actual near-limit race is covered by tests/db/tolra-ai-cap-concurrency.test.ts (two independently blocked connections), but was NOT RUN. The existing setup DB test covers cross-company admins; the new role/support contract tests do not claim live PostgreSQL policy execution. No remaining listed condition is wholly without a test; runtime DB/browser/provider proof remains open.
